flashcards.front: When should you prefer median and IQR?
flashcards.back: Prefer median and IQR when the distribution is strongly skewed or contains outliers because they are resistant summaries.

flashcards.front: What does a z-score measure?
flashcards.back: A z-score measures how many standard deviations an observation is from the mean: z = (x - mean) / standard deviation.

flashcards.front: Which design supports which conclusion?
flashcards.back: Random sampling supports generalization to a population; random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion.

flashcards.front: What is the denominator in P(A given B)?
flashcards.back: The denominator is the probability or count for condition B. Conditional probability restricts attention to the B group.

flashcards.front: What conditions define a binomial model?
flashcards.back: Use a fixed number of trials, two outcomes per trial, independent trials, and a constant probability of success.

flashcards.front: What does the Central Limit Theorem describe?
flashcards.back: For sufficiently large random samples, the sampling distribution of a sample mean can be approximately normal even when the population is not normal.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: What belongs in a confidence-interval interpretation?
flashcards.back: Name the confidence procedure, the population parameter, and the interval of plausible values. Do not describe a fixed parameter as randomly moving.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: What does a p-value mean?
flashcards.back: Assuming the null hypothesis is true, it is the probability of a result at least as extreme as the observed result.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: What does a chi-square statistic compare?
flashcards.back: It aggregates squared observed-minus-expected differences, scaled by expected counts, under a categorical null model.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: Why are t procedures used for means?
flashcards.back: The population standard deviation is usually unknown and is estimated with the sample standard deviation, adding uncertainty.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: When should measurements be paired?
flashcards.back: Use paired analysis when the same unit contributes both measurements or when observations are deliberately matched; analyze within-pair differences.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: What should a mean-inference conclusion include?
flashcards.back: State the population mean or mean difference, the direction of evidence, the statistical result, and the design limits in context.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: What is a residual?
flashcards.back: A residual is observed response minus predicted response: residual = y - y-hat. Positive residuals lie above the fitted line.
flashcards.reviewNote: Original formula and decision card; independent AP Statistics subject-expert validation remains pending.

flashcards.front: What does r-squared measure?
flashcards.back: R-squared is the proportion of observed response variation explained by the fitted linear model with the explanatory variable.

flashcards.front: What limits a regression prediction?
flashcards.back: Watch for extrapolation, nonlinear residual patterns, high-leverage points, lurking variables, and the absence of random assignment for causal claims.

memoryAids.title: Sampling versus assignment
memoryAids.content: Random sampling answers who the data can represent. Random assignment answers whether a treatment difference can support causation. A large sample does not substitute for either design feature.
memoryAids.reviewNote: Original misconception clinic; independent AP Statistics subject-expert and accessibility validation remain pending.

memoryAids.title: Conditional probability versus independence
memoryAids.content: Conditional probability changes the denominator to the condition group. Independence means the condition does not change the probability. Mutually exclusive positive-probability events are not independent.
memoryAids.reviewNote: Original misconception clinic; independent AP Statistics subject-expert and accessibility validation remain pending.

memoryAids.title: P-value versus probability of the null
memoryAids.content: A p-value is calculated under the null model; it is not the probability that the null is true. A large p-value means the data are not unusual under the null, not that the null has been proven.
memoryAids.reviewNote: Original misconception clinic; independent AP Statistics subject-expert and accessibility validation remain pending.

memoryAids.title: Paired versus independent means
memoryAids.content: Use paired analysis when each unit contributes a meaningful difference. Use a two-sample method for independent groups. Do not discard pairing by comparing the two lists as unrelated samples.
memoryAids.reviewNote: Original misconception clinic; independent AP Statistics subject-expert and accessibility validation remain pending.

memoryAids.title: Association versus regression limits
memoryAids.content: A strong r or r-squared does not establish causation. Inspect residuals, leverage, and extrapolation, and keep the study design attached to every regression conclusion.
memoryAids.reviewNote: Original misconception clinic; independent AP Statistics subject-expert and accessibility validation remain pending.

selfCheck: Use units when interpreting slope and residuals.
Treat r-squared as explained variation, not a causal probability.
Flag high leverage, nonlinearity, and predictions outside the observed range.
constructedResponseWorkshops.scoreMeaning: No score is produced. This is a planning and self-check resource, not automated FRQ scoring.
